questions.text: What are the powers and functions of the Legislative Assembly?
questions.text_as_printed: What are the powers and functions of the Legislative Assembly? (Average )

answer.value:
Powers and Functions of the Legislative Assembly:
It is the legislative body of the state.
Its decision is final in financial matters.
It exercises control over the Council of Ministers.
It has the power to remove the Council of Ministers.
Its members participate in the election of the President.

questions.text: Mention any three powers of the Governor.
questions.text_as_printed: Mention any three powers of the Governor. (Average )

answer.value:
The Governor has the executive power to appoint the Chief Minister and other Ministers of the State.
No Bill passed by the State Legislature becomes law without the Governor's assent (signature).
The Governor has financial powers, including ensuring that the State's annual budget is presented before the Legislature. A Money Bill cannot be introduced without the Governor's recommendation.

questions.text: Explain the duties of the Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs).
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the duties of the Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs). (Average )

answer.value:
Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs) make new laws and amend existing laws for the welfare of the people of the State.
They raise issues related to the development of their constituencies, such as roads, education, healthcare, and other public needs, and seek solutions from the Government.
They question the functioning of the Government during Question Hour and supervise government expenditure through discussions on the State Budget.

questions.text: What are the similarities between the Loka Sabha and the Legislative Assembly?
questions.text_as_printed: What are the similarities between the Loka Sabha and the Legislative Assembly? (Difficult)

answer.value:
Similarities between LokSabha and Legislative Assembly:
The minimum age to become a member is 25 years.
Members are directly elected by the people.
The term of office is five years.
Both are the lower houses of their respective legislatures.
Members discuss people's problems in the House.
Money bills are introduced in these houses first.
The heads of these houses are the leaders of the legislature.
Members of these houses can serve as ministers.

questions.text: What are the similarities between the Rajya Sabha and the Legislative Council?
questions.text_as_printed: What are the similarities between the Rajya Sabha and the Legislative Council? (Difficult)

answer.value:
Similarities between RajyaSabha and Legislative Council:
The minimum age to become a member is 30 years.
Members are indirectly elected.
The term of office is six years.
Both are the upper houses of their respective legislatures.
Members discuss people's problems in the House.
Eminent individuals are nominated to these houses.
Members of these houses can serve as ministers.

questions.text: What are the powers and functions of the Chief Minister?
questions.text_as_printed: What are the powers and functions of the Chief Minister? (Difficult)

answer.value:
Powers and Functions of the Chief Minister:
Advising the Governor on the appointment of ministers.
Allocating and reshuffling portfolios among ministers.
Dismissing ministers.
Playing a key role in maintaining good relations between the Centre and the state.
